name: Norwegian Fårikål
description: Fårikål, Norway's real national dish (it has its own official national day), is genuinely simple - just lamb, cabbage, whole black peppercorns, salt, and water, nothing more. Real technique layers the lamb fatty-side down in the pot, and real recipes are explicit that whole peppercorns are essential to the authentic flavor, not a garnish to skip; boiled potatoes are served drenched in the finished lamb broth.

ingredients_full.note: tsp, generous - real technique uses whole peppercorns, essential not optional

ingredients.note: tsp, generous - real technique uses whole peppercorns, essential not optional

steps_detailed: Layer the lamb, fatty-side down, in a heavy pot.
Season generously with the pepper and salt - real fårikål depends on being genuinely generous here, not restrained.
Add the cabbage wedges on top, then just enough water to reach partway up the pot.
Cover and simmer gently 1.5-2 hours, until the lamb is completely tender.
Boil the potatoes separately, then serve drenched in the lamb broth alongside.

name: Norwegian Lutefisk-Style Baked Fish
description: Real lutefisk is traditionally made from dried whitefish soaked in a lye solution over several days, a genuinely involved, caustic process that even most Norwegians skip today by buying the pre-treated fish from a shop rather than making it from scratch - this version honestly approximates only the final, simple stage: salting and baking a firm white fish until flaky.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peas, green, frozen, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peas, green, frozen, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Salt the fish and let rest, refrigerated, 2-3 hours.
Bake at 400F (200C) for 20-22 minutes, covered, until it flakes easily.
Warm the bacon and peas in a separate pan, mashing the peas roughly with the butter.
Serve the fish with the bacon and pea mash alongside.
steps: Salt the fish and let rest, refrigerated, 2-3 hours.

name: Norwegian Fiskeboller (Fish Balls)
description: Fiskeboller, real fish balls with deep Norwegian roots, real technique blending the fish very smooth so they hold together well and stay tender.
steps_detailed: Blend the fish very smooth with the egg, flour, milk, and salt.
Shape into small balls with wet hands.
Simmer in salted water 8-10 minutes until they float and are cooked through.

name: Norwegian Salmon (Grillet Laks)
description: Grilled salmon is one of the most traditional ways Norwegians prepare their most iconic export, real technique keeping the seasoning minimal so the fish's own real flavor carries the dish.
steps_detailed: Rub the salmon with the dill and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
steps: Rub the salmon with the dill and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.

name: Norwegian Waffles (Vafler)
description: Norwegian waffles are genuinely heart-shaped, not round or square, real technique using real cardamom in the batter for their distinctive aroma.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, egg, milk, cardamom, and melted butter into a smooth batter.
Cook in a heart-shaped waffle iron, 3-4 minutes, until golden.
steps: Whisk the flour, egg, milk, cardamom, and melted butter into a smooth batter.
Cook in a heart-shaped waffle iron, 3-4 minutes, until golden.

name: Norwegian Cucumber Salad
description: A simple vinegar-dressed cucumber salad with real dill, a common Norwegian side, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water.
steps_detailed: Salt the cucumber slices and let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the vinegar and sugar together, and toss with the cucumber and dill.
steps: Salt the cucumber slices and let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.

name: Norwegian Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Norway.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Norwegian Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Norwegian home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

description: A simple dill butter sauce, a common Norwegian condiment for fish.
